title: Statuspage API client: retry/backoff + idempotency keys + audit log entries
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Improves reliability of automated Statuspage updates by adding retries/backoff, idempotency keys, and an internal audit trail for publish/update actions.
description: Problem: incident-bot’s Statuspage integration currently performs best-effort POST/PATCH calls with minimal retry handling. During Sev0/Sev1s we’ve seen transient 5xx/timeout/429 responses (plus occasional network blips) leading to (a) failed publishes that require manual retry and (b) duplicate updates when a human re-triggers a step while the original request is still in flight. This PR introduces a small Statuspage API client wrapper with standardized retry/backoff, idempotency keys, and structured audit log entries for every attempted publish/update. Scope: add an HTTP client with (1) bounded retries for retryable failures (429, 5xx, network timeouts), (2) exponential backoff with jitter and respect for Retry-After where present, (3) deterministic idempotency keys so retries and replays don’t create duplicate incidents/updates, and (4) audit logging to our internal incident-bot audit sink so we can answer “what did we publish, when, and who/what triggered it?” without scraping Slack. Non-goals: changing the copy/templates (handled in PR-19344) or expanding component taxonomy fields (handled in PR-19321). Implementation details: The new StatuspageClient wraps fetch with a retry policy: max_attempts=5 (1 initial + 4 retries), base_delay_ms=250, max_delay_ms=5000, full jitter. We retry on: HTTP 429, HTTP 500/502/503/504, and network errors/timeouts. We do NOT retry on other 4xx. For 429 we honor Retry-After (seconds) if present, otherwise use computed backoff. Idempotency: we add an Idempotency-Key header on requests that create resources (incident create, incident update create). Key format is stable and derived from: statuspage_page_id, incident_id (our internal incident GUID), operation (create_incident | post_update | set_component_status), component_ids (sorted), and a normalized “update_fingerprint” (state + message hash + impact window start rounded to minute). This keeps keys stable across retries but different across meaningfully different updates. Audit log: every call to StatuspageClient emits an AuditEvent with request_id, operation, page_id, statuspage_incident_id (if known), idempotency_key, http_status, attempt_count, elapsed_ms, and redacted payload summary (we keep message length + sha256, not the full message). Audit events go to the existing incident-bot audit stream (and show up in the internal dashboard), and we also log a one-line summary to #incidents-bot-debug on failures after max attempts. Testing: added unit tests for retry classification, backoff calculations (including Retry-After), idempotency key stability, and audit event emission; added one integration-ish test that stubs the Statuspage API with a 429 then a 200 to validate behavior. Ops notes: config defaults live in statuspage_client.yaml but can be overridden via env vars for emergency tuning (MAX_ATTEMPTS, MAX_DELAY_MS).

statuspage: add idempotency key builder + header wiring
audit: add Statuspage publish/update audit events (redacted payload summary)

review_conversation: Miles Thornton (review): Retry logic looks good. Please confirm we do not retry 400/401/403/404, and ensure we only retry 429 + 5xx + network/timeouts. Also, can we cap total time spent retrying so we don’t stall incident workflows indefinitely?
Devon Price (author): Yep — only 429/5xx/timeouts. I’ll add an explicit predicate + tests for non-retryable 4xx and add a max elapsed cap (default 30s) in addition to max attempts.

Christine Wong (review): Idempotency key includes message hash + state which is great. One concern: impact window rounding to minute could cause collisions if we post multiple distinct updates within a minute with the same template message. Can we include the incident-bot timeline event id (or workflow step id) instead?

Devon Price (author): Good catch. I switched to include our internal incident_event_id when available (workflow has it); if missing, we fall back to the minute-rounded timestamp. Added a test that consecutive updates in same minute generate distinct keys when event ids differ.

Rafael Mendes (review): For audit logs, please confirm we never store the full customer-facing message. Legal asked us to avoid retaining incident copy beyond what’s already public unless needed. Message sha + length is fine. Also add page_id + statuspage_incident_id to the audit record so we can correlate quickly.
Devon Price (author): Confirmed — we only store sha256 + length, plus operation metadata. Added page_id and statuspage_incident_id fields (nullable until we get it back from create).
Allison Grant (review): Can we emit a metric for retry count / final failure so we can alert on Statuspage integration degradation? Even just a counter tagged by operation + http_status.

Devon Price (author): Added counters: statuspage_client_requests_total and statuspage_client_retries_total, plus statuspage_client_failures_total. Tags: operation, final_status (or network_error), page_id. Wired into existing metrics sink.
Miles Thornton (review): Looks solid now. Approving once the max elapsed cap lands.
Devon Price (author): Pushed follow-up commit adding max_elapsed_ms=30000 default + env override + tests. Please take another look.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Rafael Mendes. Squash commit message: "Statuspage API client: retry/backoff + idempotency keys + audit log entries"
